unit.title: Polynomial Operations and Special Products
unit.act: Act VII - Building expressions from powers
unit.role: Develop the forward multiplication machinery needed for factoring and quadratics.
unit.governingQuestion: How can expressions built from powers be combined systematically?
unit.storyArc: Polynomials are classified and evaluated, then combined through distribution. Product grids and geometry reveal special products. Division completes the reversible arithmetic of polynomials.
outcomes: Use exponent laws within monomial operations.
Recognize binomial squares and difference-of-squares products.
Perform polynomial division and verify by multiplication.
unit.investigation: Represent the same polynomial product with distribution, a product grid, and an area model.
unit.mastery: Mixed polynomial operations with missing powers, signs, and verification by reverse operations.

lessons.outcome: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form and distinguish polynomials from other expressions.

opening.prompt: Sort a collection of algebraic expressions by structure.

exposition: Identify degree, leading term, coefficients, and standard form and distinguish polynomials from other expressions. Begin by naming the mathematical objects before manipulating them. In polynomial vocabulary and evaluation, notation compresses a relationship among quantities; it does not replace that relationship. Track what each symbol represents, preserve grouping and units, and mark any restriction or endpoint as soon as it appears. The first useful question is therefore not “Which memorized move do I use?” but “What must remain true from one line or representation to the next?”

Polynomial anatomy. Read the labels as mathematical evidence: identify what is fixed, what changes, and how the objects are related. Then connect that evidence to the symbolic work one justified step at a time. A correct transformation preserves the relevant value, truth set, rate, domain, or geometric feature. If a step changes one of those, it needs a stated condition and a check against the original problem.

Exponent/coefficient sorting. Use the worked examples to compare symbolic, numerical, and visual forms. Each form should answer the same question, even when it emphasizes a different feature. Finish by interpreting the result in a complete sentence and checking it with substitution, estimation, units, graph position, or an inverse operation. That final check distinguishes a plausible-looking candidate from a supported conclusion.
